item.title: Redevelopment of St. Clare’s Convent ‘transformative’ for Kenmare
item.description: The redevelopment of St. Clare’s Convent in Kenmare will be transformative for the town. That’s according to Independent Cllr Dan McCarthy, whose proposal was given unanimous support at the recent Kenmare Municipal District meeting. The changes to the convent, which is located just outside the town, has been described as one of the biggest developments to Kenmare in many years. item.title: 26 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry
item.description: There are 26 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry today. That’s according to figures provided by the Irish Nurses and Midwives’ Organisation. 17 people are on trolleys in UHK’s emergency department, while a further 9 patients are waiting on trolleys in wards elsewhere within the hospital. Advertisement Nationally, 674 people are waiting for beds in hospitals across the country today. University Hospital Limerick is the worst affected with 118 patients on trolleys.

item.title: Search for 2026 Rose of Tralee officially underway
item.description: The search for the 2026 Rose of Tralee is officially underway. Roses and rose escorts from the 2025 edition of the festival gathered in Dublin to launch the national and international search for this year’s winner. People can now apply to become a rose or escort for this year’s festival, with rose selections taking place across more than 30 rose centres all over the world in the coming months. item.title: Ecologist accuses government of greenwashing by allowing tangle netting at Páirc Náisiúnta na Mara Ciarraí
item.description: An ecologist has accused the Government of engaging in 'greenwashing' in announcing an area of Kerry as Ireland's first marine national park. Páirc Náisiúnta na Mara, Ciarraí was announced two years ago, covering over 70,000 acres on land and sea, including land on the great Blasket Island. A new Marine Institute report found tangle netting in the area is causing serious issues for wildlife. item.title: Dingle facility formally recognised as family resource centre
item.description: For the first time, West Kerry will be served by a formally-recognised family resource centre. Dingle’s Áiseanna na hÓige childcare and family support centre has been formally admitted into the national family resource centre programme, as announced by Minister and Kerry TD Norma Foley at the Dingle centre. item.title: Ireland's flagbearers revealed for opening ceremony of Winter Olympics
item.description: Thomas Maloney-Westgard and Anabelle Zurbay will be Ireland's flagbearers at the opening ceremony of the Winter Olympics on Friday. Four athletes will represent Ireland at the Games in Milano-Cortina. Maloney-Westgard is making his third appearance at the Games, while it's an Olympics debut for Alpine skier Zurbay. item.title: Grammy winner says playing trad music in Killarney paved the way for success
item.description: A Killarney man who has been recognised for his work at the Grammys says playing trad music in his hometown paved the way for his success. Ruairí O'Flaherty from Killarney is a senior master engineer. He was part of the team which won for their work on Record of the Year, Luther, by Kendrick Lamar and SZA; this is one of the most prestigious awards at the Grammys. item.title: Two men arrested after gardaí receive report of dangerous driving in Tralee
item.description: Two men were arrested after gardaí received a report of dangerous driving in Tralee earlier today. Gardaí say they received a report of dangerous driving in the town at approximately 12 noon today. They say the vehicle crashed in the Boherbee area of Tralee, but no injuries were reported. Advertisement Gardaí say two men, aged in their 30s, were arrested at the scene and brought to Tralee garda station, where they’re currently being held this evening.
